To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The hexanucleotide expansion in chromosome 90RF72 could be associated with psychiatric presentations, (2) These presentations could be early onset, (3) The psychiatric presentations could be characterized by apathy and social withdrawal, aggressiveness, or auditory hallucinations and delirium.
we describe 3 patients carrying a hexanucleotide expansion in C9orf72 with psychiatric presentations.

the hexanuleotide repeat expansion in C9ORF2 is associated with a high number of cases of amyotrophy lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal degeneration, and that this expansion could be associated with a high prevalence of psychiatric presentations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic, clinical and pathological features of frontotemporal dementias.
the identification of the most important risk factors of the disease and the most common symptoms that appear in patients with FTD.
the study of the genetic, molecular, cellular and clinical aspects of the neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C9ORFT2 expansion is not a specific cause of FTD, but a cause of FTD and ALS with TDP-43 inclusions.
this mutation is not associated only with a motor neuron disease, but also with a behavioral variant frontotemoral dementia, and with a pure psychiatric presentation.

C9ORF 72 expansion is associated with a broad spectrum of neuropsychiatric symptoms, and that psychiatric presentations should be taken into account in the differential diagnosis of early onset behavioral variant fronto-temporal dementia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this expansion can be responsible for early onset psychiatric disorders, such as mood and behavior disturbances, and delirium, and can be associated with a lack of brain atrophy and absence of TDP-43 inclusions.

the C9ORC72 expansion could cause a spectrum of clinical phenotypes, including early-onset behavioral variant frontotemoral dementia, with or without motor neuron disease, and early-onset psychiatric presentations.
the hexanuleotide repeat expansion in C9ORF 72 could be associated with psychiatric presentations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C9ORf72 repeat expansion could be a cause of frontotemporal dementias with psychiatric symptoms.
the C9ORC72 hexanucleotid expansion should be considered as one of the causes of psychiatric presentations in young adults.
the C9ORFD72 expansion should be considered in patients with early-onset behavioral variant frontotemporai dementia, especially when there is a family history of neurodegenerative disorders.
